Required: write a meaningful imperative subject, capitalize its first letter,
and omit a final period. Keep it at most 72 characters. Use meaningful kebab-case
branch names; for an issue branch, prefix the issue number.
Recommendations: aim for at most 50 subject characters. An applicable scope
prefix is optional. Give nontrivial changes a body, separated by a blank line,
wrapped at 72 columns, with paragraphs as needed. Explain what and why rather
than narrating the diff. Describe the existing problem in present tense, why it
matters, the proposed change and why that approach helps. Avoid redundant
wording such as "currently". Split changes if the explanation becomes unwieldy.
1. Read this skill before every commit. Inspect status and both diffs first.
2. Preserve unrelated index/worktree changes. Stage named intended files only;
inspect the complete staged diff and run `git diff --cached --check`.
3. Commit each significant verified change locally. Each quality refactoring
gets its own commit and explanatory body. Include material checks/blockers.
4. Active UI failures must be fixed and rerun. Intended starter stubs may be
committed with passing foundation checks and a recorded BLOCKED UI run.
5. Never stage saved data, build output, transcripts, secrets or temporary
directories. Do not push, amend, merge or rewrite history without a new
explicit instruction. Use lightweight tags if tags are requested.
These workflow steps are project requirements, stronger than the source's
recommendations about when to include a commit body.
description: Apply the SE Education Java basic and intermediate standard to all ScheduleFlow Java production code and tests.
Required rules: use PascalCase noun type names, camelCase variables and verb
methods, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants. Keep import ordering consistent.
Attach array brackets to types. Brace loops and conditionals; put conditional
bodies on separate lines. Document classes and public methods with Javadoc;
obvious accessors, exact overrides and tests have the source's exceptions.
Start summaries with descriptive verbs; use all parameter tags or none when
names explain them. Keep comment indentation aligned.
Source recommendations: lowercase packages; English names and American
comments; mixed-case acronyms; boolean-sounding names; plural collections;
scope-appropriate names; related constant prefixes. Use four-space indentation,
eight-space continuations, K&R braces, explicit imports, local initialization
and minimal variable scope. Keep fields nonpublic except constants/data-only
types. Use whitespace around operators and after commas/keywords; separate
logical blocks. Aim below 110 columns; never exceed 120. Mark intentional
switch fallthrough. Test names may use feature_scenario_outcome.
SE rules take precedence where covered. Review the diff and run Checkstyle;
passing automation alone does not establish full compliance.

reference fields retain their null checks. Parsing and the services still own
syntax and business validation respectively. `CommandParserTest` and

`EarliestDeadlinePlanner` creates chronological half-hour slots from the
captured command time through the rolling calendar-year horizon. It excludes
recurring commitments, sorts tasks by deadline then numeric ID, and assigns
each eligible task to its earliest free slots. Overdue and out-of-horizon
tasks keep their full work estimate as unallocated; eligible tasks retain any
sessions that fit before their deadline. Adjacent slots for one task merge
within a day. Source task estimates remain unchanged.
`ScheduleService` projects the frozen plan across the complete configured daily
window. Each slot is classified as busy, assigned to a task, before the
generation cutoff, or free, in that order. Merging preserves commitment and
`ScheduleView` validate their own fields and retain immutable result lists;
allocation relationships remain the planner's responsibility. Fixed-date
planner and projection tests verify deadline order, conservation of minutes,
cutoff rounding, clipping, midnight commitments and allowed schedule dates.
`StudyWindow` validates positive same-day intervals on half-hour boundaries.
`StudyHours` holds an immutable map keyed by full lowercase weekday names or
canonical ISO dates. Resolution is date override, then weekday, then
`StudyWindow.DEFAULT` (08:00–22:00). Resets remove only the selected key.
Overnight windows and 24:00 endpoints are unsupported; the latest endpoint is 23:30.
`Snapshot` now includes `studyHours`; its original four-argument constructor
remains available and supplies defaults. Task and commitment services carry the
settings into all candidates. `SetHours`, `ShowHours` and `ResetHours` commands
use the agreed `hours TARGET /start HH:mm /end HH:mm` grammar, full lowercase
weekday names and strict ISO dates. The dispatcher saves a changed snapshot
before publication and plan invalidation; failed saves retain the old plan.
Reset dispatch uses a separate confirmation from setting hours. The renderer
identifies whether the restored window comes from a recurring weekday setting
or the default and prints its endpoints. Dispatcher tests cover both sources
and resetting an unset date; UI-015 checks the exact reset confirmations.
Both slot allocation and schedule projection resolve the window from the
snapshot. `TimeRules.eligibleStart` has a window-aware overload; the original
overload retains default behavior. `StudySession` and `ScheduleEntry` validate
same-day, positive, aligned intervals; the planner enforces configured hours.
`ScheduleView` carries and validates its effective window, retaining the original
four-argument constructor for default-window callers. Plans freeze their source
settings, so later time or unrelated snapshots do not alter projections.
The codec reads versions 1, 2 and 3. It writes version 2 when only custom hours
are present, appending sorted `HOURS|TARGET|HH:mm|HH:mm` rows. Version 3 is

its inclusive start and end date, using `-` for both endpoints of an unbounded
series in the same file. Duplicate targets,
invalid dates, unknown weekdays and invalid intervals reject the whole file.
Snapshots without custom settings retain version 1 encoding. Existing version 1
files load with defaults; older applications reject files containing newer versions.

cutoffs outside the old window. UI-015 verifies commands and persistence through

`Task` owns structural validation: positive IDs, normalized nonblank names,

overdue or out-of-horizon saved deadlines. `ValidationException` carries the
user-facing explanation and rejects a null message as programmer misuse.
`TaskService.add` checks the captured command time, accepting

are rejected before incrementing. Duplicate names are valid. Deletion removes
one known ID without resetting counters; listing returns an immutable copy in
numeric ID order and includes overdue work without reducing estimates.

### What if my work does not fit before its deadline?

Run `plan` and review the unallocated minutes and reasons. The app retains every session that fits. You can correct an estimate or deadline by deleting the task and adding a replacement, or remove a commitment if that time has become available. Run `plan` again after changes.
### How do I mark work as complete or correct an entry?
Delete completed tasks using `task delete TNUMBER`. Correct commitments with
`commitment edit CNUMBER` and one or more fields; the ID is preserved. To correct
a task, delete it and add a replacement with the correct details and a new ID.
